Jake Bauers is a Red Sox — Boston lands the Brewers' slugger on a four-year, $58 million deal

By Matt

The Red Sox have their first big bat of the winter: Jake Bauers, the Brewers' leading home run hitter and NLCS MVP, is coming to Boston on a four-year, $58 million deal, per ESPN's Jeff Passan.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The deal

First baseman Jake Bauers and the Boston Red Sox have agreed to a four-year, $58 million contract, per ESPN's Jeff Passan, who broke the news on Friday. It is the first major position-player signing of the winter, and it lands Boston the power bat it has been hunting since the offseason opened. Bauers turned 31 in October.

The Red Sox moved fast, and for good reason — the market for proven middle-of-the-order bats is thin, and Bauers just put together the best season of his career on the biggest stage in the sport.

The breakout year

2026 was the best season of Bauers' career, and it was not close. Playing for Milwaukee, he set career highs across the board and finished as the Brewers' leading home run hitter.

Slash line: .266/.389/.484

Home runs: 26

RBIs: 86

OPS+: 140

WAR: 3.3

The on-base number is the one that jumps off the page. A .389 OBP from a first baseman with that kind of power is a rare combination, and it is a big reason the price climbed into the range it did. This was not a one-month hot streak — it was a full season of production from a player who, two years ago, was thinking about walking away from baseball entirely.

The October run

Then came the postseason, where Bauers went from breakout regular-season story to October legend. He was named NLCS MVP after Milwaukee's four-game sweep of the Dodgers, hitting .286/.412/.571 in the series with six RBIs.

The at-bats told the story better than the line did. In Game 2 he ground through a 12-pitch battle with Yoshinobu Yamamoto, drawing a bases-loaded walk. In Game 3 he worked Blake Snell for 11 pitches before launching a go-ahead home run into the right-field seats. Those are the kinds of at-bats that wear down an entire pitching staff, and the Dodgers never recovered.

The sweep sent Milwaukee to its first World Series appearance since 1982, and the Brewers finished the job by beating the Rays 4-1 for the first championship in franchise history. Bauers was right in the middle of all of it.

What he brings to Boston

Boston's lineup was missing exactly this. The Sox finished 12th in the American League in home runs last season, and the front office made adding a middle-of-the-lineup hitter its offseason priority. Bauers fills the first-base power slot with a bat that gets on base, hits for power, and has now proven it plays in October.

The qualifying-offer wrinkle

One cost beyond the contract itself: Bauers received a $23.15 million qualifying offer from the Brewers, and he will turn it down to take the Boston deal. Milwaukee receives draft-pick compensation as a result.

TSL Bets: The Friday parlay (~+264) — Hawks -7.5 at the 1-9 Bulls, Grizzlies -3.5 at the Pelicans

By Matt

Two road favorites against two of the league's worst teams. Atlanta is laying 7.5 in Chicago against a 1-9 Bulls team missing its rookie highlight, and Memphis is laying 3.5 in New Orleans. Two -110 legs, about +264.

The games

Atlanta Hawks (7-5) at Chicago Bulls (1-9) — 8:00 PM ET, United Center, Chicago

Hawks -7.5 (-110), Bulls +7.5 (-110), total 245.5 (DraftKings via ESPN).

Injuries — Atlanta: Jalen Johnson is back from the left ankle sprain that cost him time — he returned Wednesday against the Wizards. Rookie point guard Kingston Flemings is questionable with a back issue; if he sits, CJ McCollum returns to the starting unit. Asa Newell is out with a toe injury, and Mouhamed Gueye, Keshon Gilbert and Henri Veesaar remain out.

Injuries — Chicago: Rookie Caleb Wilson is out after fracturing his right hand — surgery, four to six weeks, at a moment when he was playing 30.8 minutes a night and serving as the nightly highlight for the franchise. Norman Powell is questionable with a shoulder injury. Tobe Awaka is out with a back injury.

Storylines: The Hawks have won four of five and are rested, kicking off a three-game road trip still annoyed about Monday's 124-114 loss to the Lakers. The Bulls are 1-9 and coming off the worst kind of loss: they shot 85 percent in the first quarter Wednesday, built a 22-point lead against San Antonio — their largest of the season — and lost anyway. This is an NBA Cup group game, Atlanta 1-0 in East Group C, Chicago 0-1. The Hawks are the better team, the healthier team, and the team with something to prove after Monday.

Memphis Grizzlies (7-4) at New Orleans Pelicans (4-8) — 8:00 PM ET, Smoothie King Center, New Orleans

Grizzlies -3.5 (-110), Pelicans +3.5 (-110), total 235.5 (DraftKings via ESPN).

Injuries — Memphis: Zach Edey is out with an ankle injury. Scotty Pippen Jr. is out with a back injury. Quinten Post is out in concussion protocol.

Injuries — New Orleans: Trendon Watford is out with an ankle injury. Trey Murphy III, Yves Missi, Bennedict Mathurin and Bryce McGowens are all game-time decisions.

Storylines: Memphis is 7-4 and laying only 3.5 on the road against a 4-8 Pelicans team that has half its rotation on the injury report. The Grizzlies are shorthanded up front without Edey, but the Pelicans' list is longer and more important — four game-time decisions on top of an out. This is also an NBA Cup group game, and the number is small enough that Memphis does not need a statement win, just a win.

The bet

2-leg parlay (~+264): Hawks -7.5 (-110) + Grizzlies -3.5 (-110). Two road favorites against two of the league's worst teams, both laying numbers that reflect the gap rather than exaggerating it. Neither leg is a big spread — 7.5 and 3.5 — and both favorites are healthier, in better form, and playing teams whose injury reports read like a roster sheet. The Hawks are catching a Bulls team that just blew a 22-point lead at home and lost its best young player for a month. The Grizzlies are catching a Pelicans team that might not know its starting five until an hour before tip.

The honest caveat

Both legs are road favorites, and road favorites lose games they should win — Chicago is at home, desperate, and the Hawks are on the first night of a road trip with a rookie point guard who might not play. The Memphis leg is the shakier one: the Grizzlies are missing their center and two rotation players, and if Murphy and Missi both suit up for New Orleans, the Pelicans are a different team than the injury report suggests. A parlay needs both, and the second leg is the one that keeps this honest.

The pick

Hawks -7.5 + Grizzlies -3.5, about +264. A $10 ticket returns about $36.40. Two favorites, two bad teams, two small numbers.

TSL Bets: Rangers -1.5 (+114) at Canucks — the worst team in the league, and a plus-money puck line

By Matt

The Rangers are 11-8-1 and rolling into Vancouver, where the 3-16-1 Canucks are starting a .889 goalie. The puck line pays plus money. Take it.

The game

New York Rangers (11-8-1) at Vancouver Canucks (3-16-1) — 9:00 PM ET, Rogers Arena, Vancouver, ESPN+/MSGSN

Rangers -1.5 (+114), Canucks +1.5 (-135), Rangers moneyline -225, Canucks +185, total 6.5 (DraftKings via ESPN).

Goalies: Dylan Garand is expected to start for New York — 12 starts this season, 6-7-1, .905 save percentage, 2.48 goals-against average, one shutout. He has been the lead netminder since Igor Shesterkin went down with a season-ending injury six games into the year, and the Rangers have now alternated him with a returning Joonas Korpisalo, who backstopped Wednesday's 3-1 win in Calgary. Leevi Merilainen is expected for Vancouver — 2-8-1 with a .889 save percentage.

Injuries — New York: Shesterkin is out for the season. Korpisalo is back from the foot infection that sidelined him to start the year. Sean Durzi is unlikely to play after practicing in a red non-contact jersey on Thursday.

Injuries — Vancouver: Thatcher Demko is out with a hip injury. Filip Chytil is out with an upper-body injury. Tom Willander is day-to-day with a lower-body injury. Akil Thomas and Mackenzie MacEachern are out. The Canucks claimed defenseman Cameron Crotty off waivers on Wednesday.

Storylines: The gap between these teams is the whole bet. The Rangers have won two of three on their Pacific road trip, Mika Zibanejad has two goals and four assists in his last five games, Adam Fox leads the team with 22 points and Alexis Lafreniere leads it with nine goals. The Rangers are 11-1-0 when they score first and 0-7-1 when they give up the first goal — so the first goal matters more than usual here. Vancouver is 3-16-1, the worst record in the league, and its top performers over the last five games are Elias Pettersson with four assists and no goals, and Jonathan Lekkerimaki with three points. The Canucks' leading goal scorers, Brock Boeser and Lekkerimaki, have seven each — and the team has won three games all season.

The bet

Rangers -1.5 (+114). The moneyline at -225 is unplayable chalk, and the puck line is where the value lives: plus money on a good team against the worst team in the league, with a .905 goalie against a .889 one. The Rangers do not need a blowout — they need a two-goal win against a team that has managed three wins in twenty games. Vancouver has lost the kind of games where two goals is a lot to ask of the favorite, but the Canucks are not losing close — they are 3-16-1 for a reason, and the reason is in net and on the scoresheet.

The honest caveat

The Rangers are on the road at the end of a trip, and Garand is a rookie carrying a starter's load because the team's number one is done for the year. Vancouver is at home, closing a homestand, and bad teams win games they should not — the Canucks only need one good night from Merilainen and a first goal to flip the whole script, since the Rangers are 0-7-1 when they concede first. The puck line also needs a two-goal margin, and a 2-1 or 3-2 Rangers win still loses the bet. This is a bet on the gap being real, and the gap is real — but a one-goal game is always one bounce away.

The pick

Rangers -1.5 (+114). A $10 ticket returns about $21.40. The worst team in the league, a plus-money puck line, and a goalie mismatch.

Collectibles · Nov 13, 2026 · 8:00 AM ET

Delta Reign singles are spiking while Star Trek crashes on release day — this week's TCG market movers

By Matt

Pokémon's Delta Reign is a week old and its singles are climbing — Aarune up 120% in five days — while Magic's Star Trek set hits paper today with its priciest foils already down 80% from their pre-release highs.

The movers

A week into Pokémon's Mega Evolution — Delta Reign, the singles market is doing what it always does with a new set: sorting the real chases from the launch-week noise. Aarune, a holofoil at #139/103, is the week's biggest climber across every set tracked — $25.36, up from $11.52 on November 7, a 120 percent jump in five days. Kecleon, holofoil #117/103, is up 32 percent to $31.02. The sealed side is moving the other way: the Pokémon Center-exclusive Delta Reign Elite Trainer Box is down 27 percent to $152.16 from $208.63, as more boxes hit the market and the early premium bleeds off.

Magic's Star Trek set is the mirror image — and it lands on paper today. The priciest foils have already crashed from their pre-release highs: Mr. Spock, Science Officer in borderless foil is down 82 percent to $66.12 from $358.79, and General Picard, Earth Warlord in borderless foil is down 80 percent to $49 from $250. That is the normal release-week pattern — prices fall as more boxes get opened — but the scale of the drop says the pre-release market got way ahead of itself. The climbers in the set are the cheaper foils: Deep Space 9 foil is up 113 percent to $22.08, and Starbase Yorktown borderless is up 107 percent to $17.90.

The old guard is still moving, too. Sun & Moon Prism Star cards top TCGplayer's latest 30-day risers, led by Giratina ◇ from Ultra Prism — up $52.79 to $92.43 — and Base Set Unlimited Charizard is on the same list at $987.13. In the 30th Celebration set, the Mew G/RGB holofoil is up 9 percent to $3,456.93.

Release day, with a catch

Magic: The Gathering | Star Trek hits tabletop today, November 13, three days after its Arena debut. But not everything is arriving on time: Wizards says several North American products are delayed, including Commander decks, and some EMEA, Asia-Pacific and New Zealand products may also miss the launch date. Play Boosters and Prerelease Packs are on schedule — prereleases ran November 6 through 12 — so the set is playable today even where the Commander decks are late.

One more date for the calendar: Riftbound bans are announced tomorrow, November 14.

What's next

Delta Reign's singles will keep sorting themselves out over the next two weeks, and Star Trek's prices will settle once the delayed products actually land. The pattern to watch is the same one every release shows: the cards people are actually playing climb, the ones people were speculating on fall. Aarune is the first test of which kind it is.

Rockstar shared a GTA 6 clip so real-looking that fans are arguing about whether it is the game at all

By Matt

Rockstar shared a 15-second GTA 6 clip recreating a real Miami street scene in Leonida, and fans cannot agree whether they are watching gameplay, real life, or AI. The game launches November 19.

The clip

Six days before launch, Rockstar Games shared a 15-second GTA 6 clip that has the internet arguing about what it is actually looking at.

The clip started with Only in Dade, the Instagram account that posts unusual incidents from Miami-Dade County, and shows a street full of customized sports cars with people filming on their phones. Rockstar then shared it, recreating the same scene inside Leonida — the game's version of Florida — side by side with the real Miami footage the studio shot in October. The recreation is so close that viewers are debating whether they are watching actual gameplay, real-life video, or something AI-generated. Only in Dade described it as 100 percent gameplay footage, and Rockstar sharing it is the tell: this is the studio showing off its graphics, not passing off a fake video as real.

Look closely and the seams show, barely. The real clip has more people walking around; the game version has fewer pedestrians. There is also first-person footage in the comparison, which answers one open question — first-person view exists in the game for at least some of it — while leaving another open: whether the whole game can be played that way, or only while walking around and driving. November 19 is when that answer arrives.

The launch

The timing is deliberate. This is the final week of the longest marketing runway in gaming history, and Rockstar has moved from silence into a tight rollout: the 90-second launch trailer in October, pre-loading open since Tuesday, and now a clip that does not ask anyone to trust a claim about realism on faith — it shows the reference and the recreation together.

The game launches November 19 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, with no PC version announced. IShowSpeed has reportedly said he plans to travel to New Zealand to stream his first gameplay session at midnight local time on launch day, though that plan has not been officially confirmed. YouTube will run a 24-hour launch stream from midnight ET on November 19, with live gameplay and creator shows.

IShowSpeed three-peats as Streamer of the Year — Kai Cenat matches him with three awards of his own

By Matt

IShowSpeed won Streamer of the Year for the third straight time at the sixth annual Streamer Awards in Los Angeles, taking three trophies. Kai Cenat matched him with three, Jynxzi took Gamer of the Year, and Quackity received the Legacy Award.

The night

The sixth annual Streamer Awards took place Thursday night in Los Angeles, hosted by QTCinderella and Caroline Kwan — moved up a week from November 17 so it would not collide with the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI — and the two biggest names in streaming split the night right down the middle.

IShowSpeed won Streamer of the Year for the third consecutive time, beating CaseOh, Joe Bartolozzi, Jynxzi and Stable Ronaldo. He took three awards in all: the big one, Best IRL Streamer, and Best Streamed Series for his World Cup Tour. Kai Cenat matched him trophy for trophy with three of his own: League of Their Own, Best Streamed Event for Streamer University, and Best Mainstream Collab for his stream with singer Tyla.

Jynxzi was named Gamer of the Year, beating Feinberg, iiTzTimmy, supertf and TheBurntPeanut. CaseOh took Best Variety Streamer. Katie B and Vanillamace each won three as well — Katie B for Best Breakout Streamer, Best Minecraft Streamer and Best Stream Duo with Vanillamace; Vanillamace for the Sapphire Award, Best Dressed and that same duo award. Quackity received the Legacy Award. Lacy won the new Biggest Crashout award, E11ysa took Rising Star, and ashswag beat Peller and Carter Efe for Best International Streamer.

The show around the show

Thirty-seven categories were decided by a mix of fan voting — 70 percent — and an industry panel for the rest. The night also had the strangest subplot of awards season: the show's trophies were stolen from the front porch weeks before the ceremony, and the show went on anyway. For the first time, Kick streamers were eligible for nominations.

Speed's three-peat is the headline, but the balance of the night is the story — four creators walked out with three awards each, and the two men at the top of the platform split the biggest prizes between them. Nobody ran away with the show. The show is the point.

What's next

The next date on streaming's calendar is not an awards show — it is November 19, when GTA 6 launches and half the creators in that room will be live playing it. Speed has already said he plans to stream his first session from New Zealand at midnight local time.

Canadiens bury the Bruins 5-2 in Boston and take over first in the Atlantic

By Matt

Montreal scored five straight, chased Jeremy Swayman, and leapfrogged Boston for the top spot in the Atlantic. The Canadiens have points in 12 straight games. The Bruins' seven-game home win streak is over.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The night

The Montreal Canadiens walked into TD Garden, scored five straight goals, and walked out in first place. Montreal beat the Boston Bruins 5-2 on Thursday night in the first of four meetings between the Original Six rivals, leapfrogging Boston for the top spot in the Atlantic Division.

It was over early, even if the clock said otherwise. Kirby Dach opened the scoring 2:34 in, Josh Anderson made it 2-0 before the first period ended, and then the second period turned into a rout: Jake Evans scored the winner at 4:24, Cole Caufield made it 4-0 at 8:14 — and Jeremy Swayman was pulled after allowing four goals on 17 shots — and Phillip Danault added a fifth at 14:15. The Bruins were down 5-0 before the middle frame was over. Casey Mittelstadt scored both Boston goals, one late in the second and one 53 seconds into the third, but by then Montreal was in cruise control.

Jacob Fowler stopped 30 of 32 in the Montreal net for his second career win in Boston, the city where he played his college hockey. Anderson and Evans each finished with a goal and an assist.

The streak

The win runs Montreal's point streak to 12 games — 9-0-3 in that stretch — and the Canadiens have not lost in regulation in a month. They are 10-0-2 when leading after two periods, which is another way of saying that once this team gets in front, the game is basically done. Boston, meanwhile, saw its seven-game winning streak on home ice snapped, and dropped to 13-5-1 despite outshooting Montreal 32-30.

The standings flip is the headline, but the way it happened is the story: a 5-0 lead on the road in a rivalry building, against a team that had not lost at home in seven games. Montreal did not sneak past Boston. It buried them.

What's next

The Canadiens host Colorado on Saturday night. The Bruins stay home for Minnesota the same night, looking to answer the first real beating of their season.

Stephen Curry has an oblique tear — out at least two weeks, and the Warriors are bracing for a month

By Matt

An MRI confirmed an oblique abdominal tear for Stephen Curry after he left Wednesday's loss in Houston after six minutes. The Warriors say he will be re-evaluated in two weeks. ESPN reports they are bracing for closer to a month.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The news

Stephen Curry has an oblique abdominal tear, the Golden State Warriors announced Thursday, and he will be re-evaluated in two weeks. An MRI taken Wednesday night confirmed the injury. The team gave no return date — a re-evaluation is a checkpoint, not a comeback — and sources told ESPN's Shams Charania the Warriors are bracing for an absence closer to a month.

It happened fast. Six minutes into Wednesday's 115-108 loss to the Houston Rockets, Curry came off a Draymond Green screen and buried a 28-foot three, then yelled in pain after the release and signaled toward the bench. He had been grabbing at his right side for a few minutes already. He scored three points, left with 6:25 remaining in the first quarter, and did not return. Coach Steve Kerr said afterward that Curry told him it was a tweak of his side unlike anything he had felt before, and that concern was high while they waited on imaging. At halftime, before leaving the arena for the MRI, Curry spoke to his teammates and told them to focus on the task at hand.

The loss ended Golden State's eight-game win streak. The absence is the bigger story.

The stretch

At minimum, Curry misses the next seven games: at San Antonio on Friday, then New Orleans, Dallas, Memphis, Boston, Sacramento and Portland. That is the whole of the Warriors' next two weeks, and it comes with Jimmy Butler already sidelined while rehabbing the torn ACL he suffered in January. Golden State entered the stretch at 8-4, and the two players who were supposed to carry the season are both out.

The Warriors have leaned on rookies and backups before — they had to finish the Houston game that way, with Yaxel Lendeborg and Brandin Podziemski taking on the scoring and ball-handling — but this is a different test. Curry was averaging 30.6 points a game and dragging the offense with him. Without him, and without Butler, the next two weeks are about survival: stay close enough in the standings that the season is still there when the re-evaluation comes.

What's next

The first test is Friday night in San Antonio, against a Spurs team that has won 10 straight. The Warriors will get another update when Curry is re-evaluated in two weeks. Until then, the only honest timeline is the one the team gave: at least two weeks, probably more.

Daniels to Diggs with 57 seconds left — Commanders stun the Giants 24-21 on Thursday night

By Matt

Jayden Daniels threw his first two interceptions of the season, then drove Washington 71 yards in 49 seconds and hit Stefon Diggs for a 32-yard touchdown with 57 seconds left. The Commanders beat the Giants 24-21 and kept their season alive.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The night

The Washington Commanders were dead. Then they were not. Jayden Daniels marched Washington 71 yards in 49 seconds after the two-minute warning and fired a 32-yard strike to Stefon Diggs with 57 seconds left, and the Commanders stunned the New York Giants 24-21 at MetLife Stadium on Thursday night to open Week 10.

It was a strange night for Daniels. He threw his first two interceptions of the season — on back-to-back possessions — and still finished 23-of-33 for 249 yards and three touchdowns. The second pick came with the game slipping away. The answer was the drive that followed: no panic, no checkdowns, just a 71-yard march and a throw to the one receiver who has made a career out of that exact moment. Diggs finished with six catches for 83 yards and the winner. Rasul Douglas picked off J.J. McCarthy at the Washington 11 with 25 seconds left to seal it.

The Giants had the game in their hands twice. Cam Skattebo ran for 78 yards and two touchdowns and added 44 receiving yards, and with 8:13 left, McCarthy found Isaiah Likely on a crossing route that turned into a 66-yard touchdown — Likely finished with nine catches for 127 yards — to put New York up 21-17. Before that, rookie Antonio Williams had answered a Giants score with a 31-yard catch-and-run of his own, and Ben Sinnott added a touchdown grab. New York outgained Washington 399 to 340, but missed a field goal and turned it over twice.

The stakes

The loss column is what matters now. Washington improves to 3-5-1 and is two games behind the NFC East-leading Giants at 5-3-1 — and the Commanders own the tiebreaker after winning the rematch of the Week 5 meeting that ended in a 27-27 overtime tie. Washington has now gone 5-0-1 in its last six meetings with New York.

For the Giants, it is a game they had the means to win, twice, and let slip away — the kind of loss that turns a comfortable division lead into a race. For Washington, a season that looked finished at kickoff is alive again, because its quarterback threw two picks and then played the last minute like none of it happened.

What's next

Washington gets the weekend to breathe before a Week 11 trip that will decide whether this was a rescue or a stay of execution. The Giants, still on top of the East, have to answer the same question from the other side: how a 21-17 lead with eight minutes left became a loss.

Cade Cunningham drops 52 with 11 assists and zero turnovers — the first 50-10-0 game in NBA history

By Matt

Cade Cunningham scored a career-high 52 points with 11 assists and no turnovers in Detroit's 144-140 double-overtime win over Washington — the first 50-point, 10-assist, zero-turnover game since the league started tracking turnovers in 1977-78.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The night

The Detroit Pistons needed every bit of it. Cade Cunningham scored a career-high 52 points with 11 assists and no turnovers — zero, in 48 minutes — as Detroit outlasted the Washington Wizards 144-140 in double overtime at Capital One Arena on Thursday night.

He did the damage late. Thirty of the 52 came in the fourth quarter and the two overtimes, including 18 in the fourth alone. His 47th point, a three in the first overtime, tied the game at 130. He opened the second overtime with another three that put Detroit ahead for good, then buried a midrange dagger with 25.3 seconds left to make it 142-138. For the night he shot 16-for-25 from the field and 17-for-18 from the line, adding five rebounds, a steal and a block.

The Wizards kept answering. Trae Young hit a deep three at the fourth-quarter buzzer to force the first extra session, then was held to four points on 0-for-7 shooting across both overtimes. Rookie AJ Dybantsa — bloodied in a collision with Cunningham late in regulation, jaw to face — stayed in the game and sent it to a second overtime with a free-throw-line jumper with 0.1 seconds left. Washington still lost, despite 37 points and 14 assists from Young, 30 points and 15 rebounds from Anthony Davis, and 30 from Alex Sarr on 12-of-14 shooting.

Detroit got help. Ausar Thompson posted his first career triple-double — 17 points, 11 assists, 11 rebounds, four steals and three blocks — and Daniss Jenkins scored 21 for the third straight game since moving into the starting lineup. The Pistons improved to 8-3 and swept the home-and-home with Washington.

The history

According to OptaSTATS, no NBA player had ever done this before — at least not since the league started tracking turnovers in 1977-78. Plenty of stars have put up 50 and 10. Every single one of them gave the ball away at least once. Cunningham is the first to do it clean.

It is also a first inside his own franchise: no Piston had ever combined 50 points and 10 assists in a single game. And the scoring total itself is historic in Detroit — the 10th 50-point game in Pistons history, tied for the fourth-highest total ever by a Piston, behind Jerry Stackhouse's 57 in 2001, Kelly Tripucka's 56 in 1983 and Dave Bing's 54 in 1971. George Yardley also scored 52, in 1958.

The previous career high was 46 — also against the Wizards, almost exactly a year ago, on November 10, 2025. Washington has now been on the wrong end of both of his biggest nights. "It was the best I've ever done it in my NBA career for sure," Cunningham said afterward.

What's next

The Pistons are 8-3, and the 24-year-old who runs the whole thing just put up a line no one in the turnover era has ever produced. The next milestone on the board is simpler: keep winning, and let the MVP conversation come to him.

Pete Crow-Armstrong wins the 2026 NL MVP — unanimously

By Matt

All 30 first-place votes — Pete Crow-Armstrong is the 2026 NL MVP after a 40/40 season, the first ever by a Cub.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Unanimous

There was no debate. Pete Crow-Armstrong is the 2026 National League MVP, and every single BBWAA voter agreed — all 30 first-place votes, announced Thursday night. Shohei Ohtani finished second. Brice Turang was third.

At 24, the Chicago Cubs center fielder put together one of the greatest single seasons in franchise history: .280/.372/.570 (175-for-626) with 31 doubles, eight triples, 45 home runs, 41 stolen bases, 107 RBIs, 119 runs and a 157 wRC+ — and he played all 162 games. Both leagues had unanimous winners this year, with Yordan Alvarez taking the AL award the same night.

The 40/40 club

Those two numbers are the story. He became the seventh player in MLB history to record 40 home runs and 40 stolen bases in the same season — and the first Cub ever to do it. The list he joined is that short for a reason: it takes a hitter with real power and a runner with real speed, in the same body, in the same year.

The best player in baseball, by WAR

The value case wasn't close. He led all players in Wins Above Replacement — 9.8 bWAR by Baseball Reference's measure. His homer total tied Kyle Schwarber for the major-league lead, and he led the majors in runs scored and WAR. There was no argument left for anyone else by September; the vote just made it official.

Ending the Ohtani run

The win snaps Ohtani's streak of three consecutive MVP wins — 2023 in the AL with the Angels, then 2024 and 2025 in the NL with the Dodgers. Barry Bonds is the only player in MLB history to win the award in four consecutive seasons, and that record stays safe.

Head to head, it wasn't a photo finish. Ohtani hit .275 with 30 homers, 81 RBIs, 11 steals and a .889 OPS — every one of those marks sat well behind PCA's. The FanGraphs WAR gap told the same story: 10.6 to 6.6.

The turnaround

This was not a wire-to-wire coronation. Through the first six weeks he was batting just .238 with a .679 OPS, and he had one home run in the first 31 days of the season, from March 26 to April 27. The turn came in mid-May, against the Braves and 2024 Cy Young winner Chris Sale. From that matchup to the end of the season — 119 games — he slashed .294/.393/.638 with 41 homers, 31 steals and 70 walks. All of it in his second full season in the big leagues, a few months after signing a six-year, $115 million contract extension.

Ohtani's year

Part of the story is what happened on the other side. Ohtani's 2026 was injury-plagued — his first injured-list stint with the Dodgers, and a career-worst slump in September. The two-way star still put up a season most players would dream of. It just wasn't the best season in the league. Not this year.

The trophy case

The MVP is the capstone on a season that already filled a shelf: the NL Hank Aaron Award, Players Choice Player of the Year and NL Outstanding Player, the IBWAA NL MVP (457 points to Ohtani's 242), a second straight Gold Glove plus the Platinum Glove as the NL's best defender, Fielding Bible Player of the Year, and an All-MLB First Team spot.

Cubs history

He's the first Cub to win NL MVP since Kris Bryant in 2016. Bryant's win came in the middle of a World Series season. This one came in a year the Cubs' season ended early — which only underlines how undeniable the individual season was.

Yordan Alvarez wins the 2026 AL MVP — unanimously

By Matt

All 30 first-place votes — Yordan Alvarez is the 2026 AL MVP after the best season of his career.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Unanimous

There was no debate. Yordan Alvarez is the 2026 American League MVP, and every single BBWAA voter agreed — all 30 first-place votes, announced Thursday night. Junior Caminero finished second. Bobby Witt Jr. was third.

At 29, the Houston Astros slugger put together the best season of his career: .316/.432/.601 with 42 home runs, 106 RBIs, 105 runs, 34 doubles, a triple, 109 walks and a 1.033 OPS across 158 games — a career high — and 692 plate appearances. It was his first 40-homer season, and the numbers only get more absurd from there.

The best hitter in baseball, by every measure

He didn't just win his first batting title — edging Chandler Simpson's .306 — he led the American League in average, on-base percentage, slugging, OPS, total bases, walks, extra-base hits, wRC+ and OPS+. The totals behind those leads: 341 total bases, 77 extra-base hits, a 181 wRC+ and a 190 OPS+. He drew 33 intentional walks, an Astros franchise record and three shy of Aaron Judge's AL record of 36 from last year. And he was the only player in the majors all season with an OPS over 1.000.

Put simply: there was no category that mattered where he wasn't first or right there.

One short of history

He flirted with the Triple Crown all September — one homer shy of the league lead, second in RBIs. The batting title was the piece that actually landed, and it made him just the third Astro ever to win one, after Yuli Gurriel in 2021 and Jose Altuve in 2014, 2016 and 2017. His 6.8 fWAR ranked third in the majors.

The comeback

A year ago, none of this was a given. Injuries limited him to 48 games in 2025. On Wednesday night, at MLB Honors, he was named the AL Comeback Player of the Year — the night before the MVP announcement turned the comeback story into a clean sweep.

Astros history

He's the third Astro to win a BBWAA MVP, joining Jeff Bagwell (1994) and Jose Altuve (2017). Two of the three won it in the last decade, and both of them did it by being the most feared hitter in the league. Alvarez fits right in.

Entertainment · Nov 12, 2026 · 3:36 PM ET

Fat Perez, Riggs and Bobby Ray win the Internet Invitational 5 & 3

By Matt

Blue never trailed at Payne's Valley — Fat Perez, Riggs and Bobby Ray closed out Big John, Ryan Whitney and Salim 5 & 3 to split the $4 million purse and lift the Cody 'Beef' Franke Trophy.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Blue never trailed

The Internet Invitational is over, and it belongs to Team Blue. Fat Perez, Sam "Riggs" Bozoian and Bobby Ray beat Big John, Ryan Whitney and Salim Sirur 5 & 3 in the 18-hole alternate-shot final at Payne's Valley, closing the match out on the 15th hole with three still to play.

The margin tells the whole story. Blue went 1 up on the first hole and never gave it back — 2 up after three, 3 up at the turn, 4 up after ten, and 5 up after fifteen. Red never led a single hole all day. In a format built to swing wildly, with three wildly different handicaps sharing every shot, this one never really swung at all.

Each of the three winners takes home $1,338,333 from the $4 million purse, and Bobby Ray's total runs $25,000 higher — the 9th-hole money he banked alongside The Duke back on Day 2. On top of the split, the trio also takes home a Tracker boat from Bass Pro Shops. The trophy they lifted is the Cody "Beef" Franke Trophy, named for last year's winner.

The drama: Salim, and the finale nobody could look away from

The score says Blue won 5 & 3. The internet says something else decided it — or at least ruined the watch. Salim Sirur, Red's third man, drank through the episode on camera: a tequila shot on just about every hole, beers on top of it, asking the cart girl for another round. Australian Golf Digest's episode recap named him "the drunkest man alive" and described him as "blackout drunk" going into the final, showing no signs of stopping.

It bled into the team. At one point Salim took a beer out of Big John's hand, causing real friction inside the group, and Ryan Whitney spent part of the match coaching Big John on keeping Salim's vibes up rather than letting it show. Big John, for his part, came out of it as the sympathetic figure of the finale — viewers calling him "all heart" and the MVP of a losing team.

The audience reaction has been brutal. Across Barstool's, Portnoy's and the Invitational's own posts, the comments are dominated by viewers calling the finale unwatchable, blaming Salim's drinking for costing his teammates $1.3 million each, and calling for him not to be invited back. Some of it is cruel; a smaller thread defends him or jokes about it. The dominant tone is anger that a $4 million match came down to a guy who could barely stand up straight.

There is a twist that complicates the whole thing: Salim himself has said he's on Day 87 of a 90-day sober challenge — he knew before the episode aired that he needed a lifestyle change. Golf Digest called the whole thing "an all-time drunk golf performance" while noting he's since reeled the drinking in. Whether the finale becomes a turning point for him or just the episode everyone remembers him for is the open question hanging over next year.

The trophy means something

That name is the emotional center of this whole series. Cody "Beef" Franke won the first Internet Invitational in 2025 alongside Brad Dalke and Francis Ellis, beating Paige Spiranac, Frankie Borrelli and Malosi Togisala 1 up in the final. He died suddenly at 31 in October 2025, the day before the series aired. Barstool and the Fore Play crew helped set up a scholarship fund in his name at his alma mater, Ferris State, and his family opened this year's first episode to introduce the Beef Franke Foundation, which funds golf-management scholarships and a Heart of the Course Award for the people who keep courses running. They finished by teaching the room Beef's signature send-off: two claps and a woo.

So when the trophy got handed over at Payne's Valley, it wasn't just a prop with a funny name. It was the whole point of the week.

How Blue got here

Nobody had this trio winning it when the field of 64 was drafted. All six finalists came out of Ryan Ruffels' Team White, which survived a wild three days at Big Cedar Lodge in Ridgedale, Missouri.

Day 1 at Ozarks National ended with Ruffels and Peter Finch's team tied 8–8, and Ruffels going through on a sudden-death playoff — Big John, nearly left out of the event entirely, holing the putt on the second extra hole. Defending champions Dalke's Red lost 10.5–5.5 to Wesley Bryan's Green and went home. Day 2 at Buffalo Ridge was sixteen singles matches, and Ruffels closed it out 12.5–6.5, with Salim winning the 17th and 18th to clinch it on the last.

Then came the twist: four of Ruffels' sixteen were going home that night. The captains played a sudden-death hole under the lights, and Grant Horvat's team went out when Ryan Whitney's par beat Jake Adams on the next hole — taking Horvat, Adams, Spiranac and Jon Gruden with it. The last twelve were split into four teams of three for nine holes of alternate-shot stroke play at Payne's Valley, top two through. Blue won it at two over. Red got through at four over only because Salim holed a bogey putt on the last that would have tied Green if he'd missed.

On paper, the final was close: Blue's combined handicap averaged 2.1 (Fat Perez 0.3, Riggs 4.1, Bobby Ray 2.0) against Red's 2.9 (Big John +3.1, Whitney 2.1, Salim 9.8). A million simulations gave Blue a 57% edge. On the course, it wasn't close at all.

What this event is

For anyone still catching up: the Internet Invitational is Barstool Sports and Bob Does Sports' creator golf tournament, hosted by Dave Portnoy, who runs the show as host and rules commissioner alongside Big Cat and former PGA Tour pro Kevin Kisner. The second edition filmed August 10–17, 2026 at Big Cedar Lodge and rolled out in six episodes on YouTube — Mondays and Thursdays, October 26 through today — free on the Fore Play Golf, Bob Does Sports and Internet Invitational channels, presented by Dunkin'.

The first two episodes alone drew more than 16 million combined views. It's the rare YouTube golf series that plays like a real sports event: a draft, team play, a rules committee with actual teeth — the "Gruden Rule" lets them veto any pairing that looks like a thrown match — and side pots everywhere, including a $500,000 Reese's hole-in-one prize on the par 3 each day and $25,000-a-man payouts on the Day 2 9th hole. The production team cut it from more than 24 terabytes of raw footage, and the 2025 series was a Shorty Awards finalist for Best Video Series.

It also never stops being messy, which is half the appeal. The Duke, the weakest golfer in the 64-man field, became the story of Episode 5 when his play cost Ruffels and Marissa Wenzler their shot at the final — then took to Instagram to apologize to his teammates. Portnoy spent Wednesday addressing whether The Duke gets invited back at all.

What's next

Portnoy has confirmed the Invitational will be an annual event, and the 2026 edition proved the format has legs: a bigger field, a purse four times the size of year one, and a final that delivered a clean, decisive winner. The champions list now reads two lines long — Dalke, Ellis and Beef in 2025; Fat Perez, Riggs and Bobby Ray in 2026. Three guys who started the week as long shots walk away as millionaires, and the trophy they lifted carries the name of the guy who won it first.

Streamer Awards go live tonight in Los Angeles

By Matt

Streaming's biggest night is tonight — the sixth annual Streamer Awards, live free on Twitch and YouTube, with IShowSpeed, Jynxzi, and Kai Cenat leading the nominations and one very stolen set of trophies hanging over the show.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

Streaming's biggest night

The Streamer Awards go live tonight from Los Angeles, with the main show at 8:30 p.m. ET streaming free on Twitch and YouTube. The red carpet starts at 5:30 p.m. ET, and the whole night is hosted by the show's founder, QTCinderella, alongside Caroline Kwan.

This is the sixth edition of the show, and the largest one yet: 37 categories covering creators across Twitch, YouTube, and Kick. Fan voting counted for 70% of each result, with an industry panel deciding the remaining 30%. Voting ran October 16 through October 31, so tonight is purely about the reveals.

The names to watch

IShowSpeed, Jynxzi, and Kai Cenat lead the field with four nominations each. Speed is the defending Streamer of the Year, and he is on the ballot again — joined by CaseOh, Joe Bartolozzi, Jynxzi, and Stable Ronaldo in the flagship category, presented by YouTube this year.

Kai Cenat's four nominations all sit outside that flagship race: the two-time past winner is not on the Streamer of the Year ballot at all, which was one of the biggest talking points when the nominees were revealed on October 16. The other one was xQc, who got zero nominations across all 37 categories and spent the night voting for Speed instead.

Beyond the top prize, the marquee races include Best Marathon Stream — Speed and Kai's Minecraft Marathon against Cinna's Cinnathon, DDG's Hit-A-Thon, JasonTheWeen's 7 Days Stranded, and the Chained Together run from Jynxzi, Stable Ronaldo, and LosPollosTV — plus Streamer University, Kai's summer event, up for Best Streamed Event.

The trophies were stolen

Yes, really. On October 29, QTCinderella announced on X that this year's trophies had been stolen off one of the show's producers' front porches after delivery, and asked anyone in the Los Angeles area who spots them at a Goodwill or pawn shop to let her know. The good news for the results: winners' nameplates aren't attached until the night before the ceremony, so nothing was spoiled — the thief got a box of very blank trophies. QT joked the winners' plates might end up on coffee mugs instead.

The show itself was also moved up a week, from November 17 to tonight, to get clear of the GTA VI release. And for the first time, Kick streamers were eligible for nominations this year.

How to watch

The red carpet starts at 5:30 p.m. ET and the main ceremony follows at 8:30 p.m. ET, streaming free on QTCinderella's Twitch and YouTube channels. Co-streaming is open to everyone — QT confirmed on November 11 that all co-streams are welcome, on any platform, as long as "Streamer Awards" is in the title.

MLB · Nov 12, 2026 · 8:08 AM ET

Red Sox inquire about Seiya Suzuki

By Matt

Boston has checked in on free agent Seiya Suzuki, per Pete Abraham — the Cubs slugger is coming off the best season of his career and would add the power bat the Sox lineup lacked.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The first bat checked

The Red Sox have checked in on free agent Seiya Suzuki, according to Pete Abraham of the Boston Globe. Free agency opened on November 2, and Suzuki is the first premier bat Boston has reportedly asked about.

The inquiry came out of the GM Meetings in Las Vegas, where Abraham also reported the worst-kept secret in the room: Boston is shopping left fielder Jarren Duran. The two moves fit together — if Duran goes, there's an outfield spot and a middle-of-the-order hole to fill, and Suzuki is the top right-handed bat on the market.

What Suzuki did in 2026

Suzuki, 32, just finished the best season of his five-year run with the Cubs. He set a career high with 5.1 wins above replacement while playing 143 games, and he did it as the middle-of-the-order bat Chicago leaned on all year.

Games: 143

Slash line: .270/.368/.473

Home runs: 26

Doubles: 31

RBIs: 86

OPS: .841

That production is exactly what Boston's lineup was missing. The Sox finished 12th in the American League in home runs last season, and the front office has made adding a middle-of-the-lineup hitter its offseason priority. This isn't the first time the two sides have been linked, either — The Athletic's Jen McCaffrey named Suzuki as a possible Boston target last week.

What it would cost

Suzuki just completed a five-year, $85 million deal he signed with the Cubs ahead of the 2022 season. Chicago extended him a one-year, $23.1 million qualifying offer, but his agent, Joel Wolfe, said at the GM Meetings that Suzuki will decline it and test the open market.

The early projections put the price in nine figures: Spotrac projects a four-year deal worth just over $109 million, while The Athletic's Jim Bowden projects five years and $120 million. Boston won't be bidding alone — the Mariners, Padres, Phillies and Blue Jays are all reported to have interest, and the Cubs are expected to make an effort to keep him.

There's also a draft-pick cost attached. Because Suzuki received a qualifying offer, signing him would cost Boston a second- and fifth-round pick in the 2027 MLB Draft plus $1 million in international signing bonus pool space.

TSL Bets: The Thursday parlay (~+550) — Kaprizov to score, Wild moneyline, Avalanche-Senators Over 6.5

By Matt

Three legs, three different bets: Kirill Kaprizov to score in Toronto, the Wild to beat a reeling Leafs team, and goals in Ottawa where the over is 9-1 in the last ten meetings. About +550.

Leg 1: Kirill Kaprizov anytime goal (+105)

Minnesota Wild (13-3-4) at Toronto Maple Leafs (8-10-2) — 7:00 PM ET, Scotiabank Arena, Toronto

Wild -170, total 6.5.

Injuries — Minnesota: Filip Gustavsson is on injured reserve with a hip injury. Brock Faber is out with a skull fracture — he has resumed skating but is not expected back until Saturday. Jared Spurgeon is out with a lower-body injury. Michael McCarron is questionable with an upper-body injury.

Injuries — Toronto: Morgan Rielly could return after missing two games with a lower-body injury. Kirill Marchenko and Colton Sissons remain sidelined with lower-body injuries. Max Domi, Miles Wood, Nick Blankenburg, Elvis Merzlikins, Cade Webber, Marshall Rifai and William Villeneuve are all out.

Storylines: Kaprizov has 17 goals — second in the NHL — and 32 points in 20 games. He has scored in five of the Wild's last six road games, and he scored the overtime winner 21 seconds in at Montreal on Tuesday, extending Minnesota's point streak to nine games. The Leafs have lost four straight, allowed 17 goals four games into a six-game homestand, and are still looking for their first win of November. Backup Anthony Stolarz could get the nod in net, with the starter having lost five straight. Kaprizov against a battered Toronto defense is the best goalscorer bet on the board tonight.

Leg 2: Wild moneyline (-170)

Same game, same reasoning, different bet. Minnesota is 13-3-4, riding a nine-game point streak, with the league's second-leading goalscorer and a defenseman in Quinn Hughes who just became the second-fastest blueliner in league history to 80 points with a franchise — 68 games. Toronto is 8-10-2, has lost four straight, and is missing half its defense corps. The Wild are road favorites for a reason, and the -170 is the price of betting the best form in the league against the worst.

Leg 3: Avalanche at Senators Over 6.5 (+100)

Colorado Avalanche (11-6-2) at Ottawa Senators (11-6-2) — 7:00 PM ET, Canadian Tire Centre, Ottawa

Avalanche -120, total 6.5, Over +100 (Fanatics).

Injuries — Colorado: Josh Manson is on injured reserve (long-term) and Zachary L'Heureux is on injured reserve. Nathan MacKinnon is healthy and leads the team with 30 points.

Injuries — Ottawa: Andre Burakovsky, Warren Foegele and William Eklund are on injured reserve. Nick Cousins is out. Linus Ullmark is day-to-day with a lower-body strain — he is 7-1-0 with a 1.33 goals-against average and a .945 save percentage when he plays, which is exactly why this leg carries a warning label.

Storylines: The over is 13-6 in Colorado games this season, and 9-1 in the last ten meetings between these two teams. The Avalanche average 4.11 goals a game, just won 6-3 in Toronto for their second straight win, and have scored 10 goals in two games. Ottawa lost 3-2 in overtime to Washington on Tuesday and is banged up up front. If Ullmark plays, the over gets harder — he is the best goalie in this matchup by a wide margin. If he sits, two offenses that score for fun get a backup. Either way, seven goals is the number, and these two teams have cleared it in nine of their last ten meetings.

The bet

Parlay: Kaprizov anytime goal (+105) + Wild moneyline (-170) + Avalanche-Senators Over 6.5 (+100) — about +550.

A prop, a favorite, and a total — three different kinds of bets, and none of them copies a single from today. The Kaprizov goal and the Wild moneyline are correlated, which is the point: if Minnesota wins in Toronto, the odds are good that Kaprizov is the reason. The over is the independent leg, and it is built on the strongest totals trend on the board tonight.

The honest caveat

Two of the three legs live in the same game, so a bad night in Toronto kills the ticket twice over. Kaprizov can be held off the scoresheet — it happens to everyone — and the Wild are missing their starting goalie and their best defenseman. The over is the riskiest leg on its own terms: if Ullmark plays, a 1.33 goals-against average is a real obstacle to seven goals. A parlay is a parlay: three things have to go right, and one of them is a goalie decision nobody has confirmed yet. Bet accordingly.

The pick

Kaprizov anytime goal + Wild moneyline + Avalanche-Senators Over 6.5 — about +550. A $10 ticket returns about $65. A scorer, a favorite, and the best over trend on the board.

TSL Bets: Bruins moneyline (-128) vs Canadiens — 8-1 at home against a banged-up rival

By Matt

Boston is 13-4-1, 8-1-0 at home, and allowing 2.3 goals a game. Montreal hasn't lost in regulation in a month — but the Habs are without Demidov and their goalie picture is unsettled. Take the Bruins at home.

The game

Montreal Canadiens (11-3-4) at Boston Bruins (13-4-1) — 7:00 PM ET, TD Garden, Boston, ESPN+

Bruins moneyline -128, Canadiens +106, total 6.5 (FanDuel).

Injuries — Boston: James Hagens is on injured reserve, est. return November 21. That is the whole list — the Bruins are otherwise healthy.

Injuries — Montreal: Ivan Demidov is on injured reserve with an ankle injury, est. return November 14 — he has played two games all season. Mike Matheson is day-to-day with a lower-body injury. Samuel Montembeault is on injured reserve, with a return imminent. Nick Suzuki and Jake Evans both missed Wednesday's practice for treatment, with no diagnosis and no timeline given. Jacob Fowler has taken the number one job in net: 8-1-2, 2.14 goals-against average, .925 save percentage.

Storylines: This is first against second in the Atlantic — Boston with 27 points, Montreal with 26 — and both teams are playing well. The Bruins have won eight of nine home games and are giving up only 2.3 goals a game, with eight forwards at 10-plus points and 5-plus goals. The Canadiens have points in 11 straight games (8-0-3), have not lost in regulation since October 14, and are 6-1-1 on the road. Lane Hutson leads them with 18 points, Cole Caufield has 11 goals, and Nick Suzuki has 16 points. Boston has won seven of the last ten meetings, and five of the last six in Boston. The models split the difference — one has Boston at 65% to win, the market has it closer to a coin flip, and the -128 sits in between.

The bet

Bruins moneyline (-128). Home ice, the healthier roster, the better defense, and a head-to-head edge in this building. Montreal's point streak is real, but it is built on overtime and shootout points as much as wins — and the Habs are doing it without their best young forward, with a day-to-day top defenseman and a goalie situation that is still sorting itself out. Boston at -128 is a fair price for the better team at home.

The honest caveat

Montreal has not lost in regulation in a month, and Fowler is not a backup playing above his head — he is 8-1-2 with a .925 save percentage and has taken the job outright. The Canadiens are 6-1-1 on the road, they score 3.5 goals a game, and this is a rivalry game where the records barely matter. If Suzuki and Evans are fine after their treatment day, the Habs are close to full strength at forward. The -128 is a fair price, not a steal — this is a bet on home ice and health, and both of those edges are real but thin.

The pick

Bruins moneyline (-128). A $10 ticket returns about $17.81. The healthier team, at home, with the better defense.

TSL Bets: Giants -2.5 (-110) vs Commanders — the healthier team, at home, in a rematch

By Matt

The Giants are 5-2-1, 6-2 against the spread, and getting Cam Skattebo back with J.J. McCarthy expected to play. Washington is 2-5-1, without McLaurin for the season and Tunsil on IR. Lay the 2.5 at home.

The game

Washington Commanders (2-5-1) at New York Giants (5-2-1) — 8:15 PM ET, MetLife Stadium, East Rutherford, NJ, Prime Video

Giants -2.5 (-110), moneyline Giants -134, total 41.5 (DraftKings via ESPN).

Injuries — Washington: Terry McLaurin is out for the season. Tackle Laremy Tunsil is on injured reserve until around December. Guard Lucas Patrick is doubtful with a concussion. Wide receiver Treylon Burks is questionable with a foot injury and tight end Colson Yankoff is questionable with a knee injury. Jacory Croskey-Merritt is on injured reserve and Jeremy McNichols is out for the year, leaving the backfield thin. Jayden Daniels has a left elbow issue but practiced fully on Monday and Tuesday.

Injuries — New York: Quarterback J.J. McCarthy is expected to play despite the hip pointer he suffered against Philadelphia — he missed 16 snaps in the third quarter but was a full participant in practice Tuesday. Running back Cam Skattebo, who missed the Philadelphia game with a hamstring issue, was also full Tuesday and is expected to be full go. Both starting cornerbacks are out: Paulson Adebo and Jarrick Bernard-Converse are on injured reserve, and Trey Amos is on IR for Washington as well.

Storylines: These two played to a 27-27 overtime tie on October 11, after Washington let a 27-13 fourth-quarter lead slip away — and a Skattebo fumble in overtime cost the Giants a win. The winner on Thursday takes the head-to-head tiebreaker and the NFC East lead. The Giants are 6-2 against the spread this season, including 3-1 at home, and rookie linebacker Arvell Reese was just named NFC Defensive Player of the Week after 12 tackles, three sacks and a forced fumble against the Eagles. Daniels has not thrown an interception this year and has nine total touchdowns, but the Commanders have won only one game he has started, and Myles Garrett sacked him three times last week. The total has fallen from 47.5 at open to 41.5 — the market expects a grind, in the rain (67% chance of precipitation, 53°F at kickoff).

The bet

Giants -2.5 (-110). The healthier offensive line, the more reliable run game, the better defense, and home field in a short-week divisional rematch. Skattebo ran for a season-high 188 yards against Houston in Week 7, and Washington's run defense has to deal with him behind a line that is intact — while the Commanders' line is missing its left tackle and possibly its left guard, with their best receiver out for the year. Lay the 2.5.

The honest caveat

McCarthy is playing hurt, and the 16 snaps he missed against Philadelphia showed what the offense looks like without him — 3 of 7 for 26 yards. Daniels has not thrown a pick all season, and divisional Thursday games are weird by nature; the first meeting ended in a tie, which tells you how close these teams are. The rain and the short week cut both ways, and the total dropping six points says the market thinks points will be scarce — a low-scoring game makes 2.5 a bigger number than it looks. But the Giants are the better team right now, and the injuries say so even more loudly than the record does.

The pick

Giants -2.5 (-110). A $10 ticket returns about $19.09. Healthier, at home, with the better run game — lay the small number.

Collectibles · Nov 12, 2026 · 7:55 AM ET

Pokémon's Day & Night boxes are trading at double retail a week after launch — and the market is already cooling

By Matt

The Pokémon TCG 30th Celebration Ultra-Premium Collections — Day with Espeon ex, Night with Umbreon ex — launched November 6 at $179.99. Pre-release market prices ran past three times retail, and even after a pullback they are still trading well above it.

The boxes

The peak product of Pokémon's 30th anniversary year landed on November 6: the 30th Celebration Ultra-Premium Collections, in two versions — Day, built around Espeon ex, and Night, built around Umbreon ex. Each one retails for $179.99 at the Pokémon Center and participating retailers.

What is inside justifies the price tag, at least on paper. Every box carries 30 packs — 29 from the 30th Celebration set plus one Classic Collection pack with three etched cards from the anniversary subset, including the Base Set Charizard reprint. Then the promos: a foil Pikachu ex illustrated by YOSHIROTTEN in a day or night version, and a foil Espeon ex or Umbreon ex depending on the box. A playmat, deck box, 65 sleeves, a metal coin and six damage-counter dice round it out.

The two versions are identical except for the theme — the featured Eeveelution, the Pikachu art, and the accessories. Espeon and Umbreon are the Gen II Eeveelutions, the pair that has anchored Pokémon collecting since Gold and Silver, and the 30th anniversary is the first time they have headlined a premium box together.

The market

The resale market did what it always does with a premium Eeveelution product: it went vertical, then started coming back down.

TCGplayer's pre-release market figures put both versions at more than three times retail — roughly 3.1 times for Day and 3.3 times for Night. At launch, market tracking had both boxes above $420. But the peak is already behind us: in the week before launch, Night fell 25% and Day fell 22.6% from their highs, as supply actually reached shelves.

Good luck choosing, though. Best Buy listed the collections with a one-per-order restriction and assigns buyers a random Day or Night version rather than letting them pick. In France, only Night released on November 6 — Day is expected November 27.

Why it matters

The 30th Celebration set itself launched September 16 — all-foil cards, 30 unique Pikachu cards with one guaranteed in every booster, a new Futuristic Rare rarity. The Day & Night boxes are the anniversary's premium capstone, and the Classic Collection pack inside is the only place to pull those gold-bordered reprints of three decades of icons.

The market cooling off a pre-release spike is normal. The question is where the floor is: at $179.99 retail with 30 packs and two exclusive promos, the box is fairly priced even before resale. If you can find one at retail, that is the buy. If you are paying $420, you are paying for the Eeveelutions, not the cardboard.

Gaming · Nov 12, 2026 · 7:55 AM ET

Resident Evil Requiem takes Game of the Year at the Golden Joysticks — and a two-person indie matched it

By Matt

Capcom's Resident Evil Requiem won Ultimate Game of the Year at the 44th Golden Joystick Awards in London. The night's other story: Meccha Chameleon, made by two people in five months, won four awards — the most ever by an indie at the ceremony.

The night

The 44th Golden Joystick Awards took over the Troxy in London on Wednesday night, and the headline result went the way most people expected: Resident Evil Requiem is the Ultimate Game of the Year.

Capcom's survival-horror sequel did not just win the big one. It took Console Game of the Year, Best Game Trailer and Best Lead Performer for Angela Sant'Albano as Grace Ashcroft — four awards for one game, and seven for Capcom overall, including Studio of the Year. PRAGMATA and Onimusha: Way of the Sword added to the haul. Requiem has now sold 8.5 million copies.

The rest of the major prizes spread out: Crimson Desert won PC Game of the Year, The Witcher 4 took Most Wanted Game, CONTROL Resonant won Best Visual Design and Onimusha took Best Audio Design. The show also premiered the announcement trailer for Conan: The Black Pyramid, a roguelite action RPG with two-player online co-op, planned for PC in 2027.

The other winner

The best story of the night was not the favorite winning. It was the tie.

Meccha Chameleon — a hide-and-seek party game made by two people, Lemorion and Haganeiro, in roughly five months — also won four awards, matching Requiem for the most on the night. It beat Marathon, Valheim and ARC Raiders for Best Multiplayer, topped Mewgenics and Cairn for Best Self-Published Indie, and won the Developers' Choice award over Mortal Shell 2 and Orbitals. It won every category it was nominated in except Best PC Game, which went to Crimson Desert.

Those four wins are the most any indie game has ever taken home from a single Golden Joystick ceremony in the awards' 44-year history. The game has sold more than 20 million copies — more than Pokémon Legends Z-A, God of War Ragnarök and Resident Evil Village managed in their lifetimes.

One more record fell on the night: with its Best Remake/Remaster win, The Witcher 3 now has 10 Golden Joystick wins in total, the most of any game in the ceremony's history.

The fine print

The Golden Joysticks run early in the fall, and the cutoff shows: November releases like the Ocarina of Time remake and Grand Theft Auto VI were not eligible for Ultimate Game of the Year. The Game Awards, the other big show of the season, is still to come — and those two games will be very much in that conversation.

Sports · Nov 12, 2026 · 7:54 AM ET

Kucherov's natural hat trick buries Buffalo — and Carlson hits 800 points on the same play

By Matt

Nikita Kucherov scored a natural hat trick in the third period as Tampa Bay beat Buffalo 8-3. John Carlson had five points in the win, and his assist on Kucherov's third goal was the 800th point of his career.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The night

The Tampa Bay Lightning led Buffalo 4-0 midway through the second period on Wednesday night, and then nearly gave the whole thing away. The Sabres scored three straight — Josh Doan and Jason Zucker late in the second, Tage Thompson 33 seconds into the third — and a blowout was suddenly a one-goal game at KeyBank Center.

Then Nikita Kucherov did what he does.

Fifty-two seconds after Thompson's goal, Kucherov went in alone on a breakaway and beat Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen with a backhand under his left arm to make it 5-3 — ending Luukkonen's night in the process. At 4:11 he one-timed a John Carlson feed from the right circle to make it 6-3. At 14:13, from the same spot, on the power play, off another Carlson feed, he completed the natural hat trick: three goals, one period, no one else scoring in between. Brandon Hagel added his second of the night at 15:06 for the 8-3 final.

Kucherov finished with three goals and an assist. Carlson finished with a goal and four assists — five points — and the assist on the hat-trick goal was the 800th point of his NHL career. Jake Guentzel added four assists of his own, Anthony Cirelli had three, and Andrei Vasilevskiy made 28 saves. Tampa Bay improved to 12-4-2 and is 5-1-2 in its last eight. Buffalo fell to 8-7-3, losers of three of four.

The history

The natural hat trick was the third of Kucherov's career — the most in Lightning history. It was his eighth hat trick overall, tying Martin St. Louis for the second-most in franchise history. Steven Stamkos, with 13, is the only name ahead of him.

Carlson's milestone landed on the same play, which is fitting: 800 career points (176 goals, 624 assists) for a defenseman who has spent his whole career setting up exactly that kind of goal. "Nothing he does surprises me now," Carlson said of Kucherov afterward. Coach Jon Cooper was blunter: "'Kuch' did a Kuch thing."

It is worth remembering where this story was a week ago. Kucherov scored the overtime winner against Minnesota on Sunday, seven days after his trade request became public — and then made it clear, again, that he intends to keep playing for the Lightning. A natural hat trick in a game his team nearly let slip is the loudest possible version of that message.

The fine print

Two footnotes from a wild night in Buffalo: rookie Sam O'Reilly, making his NHL debut, picked up his first career point with the secondary assist on Yanni Gourde's goal. And defenseman Erik Cernak left the game in the second period after colliding with the curved glass — Cooper said he is "probably out tomorrow" when Tampa Bay visits Columbus on Thursday. Cirelli played his 600th NHL game.

Sports · Nov 12, 2026 · 7:54 AM ET

Macklin Celebrini is the fifth-youngest player ever to 200 points — and he did it in a loss

By Matt

Macklin Celebrini scored his 200th career point at 20 years and 151 days old — fifth-youngest in NHL history, behind only Crosby, Gretzky, Carson and Lemieux — then added his 201st in the same game.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The night

The San Jose Sharks lost 3-2 in a shootout to the Pittsburgh Penguins on Wednesday night at SAP Center, blowing a game they had clawed back from 2-0 down in the third period. Ben Kindel scored in regulation and had the lone shootout goal for Pittsburgh. Sergei Murashov made 34 saves for the Penguins.

But the night belonged to the losing captain anyway.

With just over eight minutes left in the third, Macklin Celebrini broke up Murashov's shutout, pulling San Jose within one. That goal was the 200th point of his NHL career, in his 171st game. Four minutes later he added his 201st, the primary assist on Mason Marchment's tying goal — Marchment's 100th career goal.

The history

At 20 years and 151 days old, Celebrini is the fifth-youngest player in NHL history to reach 200 career points. The four names ahead of him are the entire argument for why this matters: Sidney Crosby (19 years, 207 days), Wayne Gretzky (19 years, 347 days), Jimmy Carson (20 years, 107 days) and Mario Lemieux (20 years, 133 days).

He is also just the 14th player ever to pass the 200-point mark before turning 21, and the fifth-fastest active player to get there. Within his own franchise, the pace is unmatched — no player who began his career with the Sharks has ever reached 200 points this fast. The previous franchise mark belonged to Logan Couture, who needed 273 games. Celebrini did it in 171.

The context around him makes it louder. Celebrini is the No. 1 pick of the 2024 draft, the youngest captain in Sharks history and the sixth-youngest captain in NHL history. In July he signed a five-year, $94 million extension — $18.8 million a year — starting in 2027-28. San Jose has already decided what he is. Nights like this one are the receipt.

What's next

The Sharks hit the road Saturday at Utah. The milestone watch is over; the next one is 300, and at this pace it is not that far away.

The Warriors' win streak is over — and Curry left after six minutes

By Matt

Houston beat Golden State 115-108 on Wednesday, ending the Warriors' eight-game win streak. Stephen Curry played six minutes before leaving with right abdominal soreness, and the MRI results weren't known after the game.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The night

The Houston Rockets beat the Golden State Warriors 115-108 on Wednesday night in Houston, and the final score only tells half of it. The Warriors' eight-game winning streak — the run that started after an 0-3 opening and made them the first team ever to open a season with three losses and then win eight in a row — is over.

The bigger worry left the floor in the first quarter. Stephen Curry played six minutes before departing with right abdominal soreness. He underwent an MRI after the game, and the results weren't immediately known, coach Steve Kerr said postgame. Golden State played most of the night without the player carrying the streak — Curry was averaging 30.6 points a game, 32.3 over his last five.

Houston did not need a masterpiece to close it out. Alperen Sengun flirted with a triple-double — 19 points, 13 rebounds, nine assists — Kevin Durant led the Rockets with 20, and Amen Thompson added 19 points and seven rebounds. The Rockets pulled away in the fourth quarter for their second straight win, improving to 9-3. Golden State falls to 8-4.

Why it matters

Streaks end. That is the boring part. The interesting part is how this one ended — not with a cold shooting night or a buzzer-beater, but with the best player on the floor walking to the locker room six minutes in and the team holding on for three quarters before Houston's depth took over.

The Warriors have been shorthanded all through the run — Jimmy Butler, Moses Moody and Gary Payton II are all out — and they kept winning anyway. But there is shorthanded and then there is no Curry at all, and Wednesday was the second one. Until the MRI results come back, the streak is the smaller story. The abdominal is the story.

Around the league

Boston pulled off its own 22-point comeback on the same night, beating Toronto 98-93 behind Jayson Tatum's 24 — the Celtics' fifth straight win. James Harden scored a season-high 32 as Cleveland won 115-107 at the Garden.

Spurs win their 10th straight after erasing a 22-point hole in Chicago

By Matt

Victor Wembanyama scored 32 and Dylan Harper added 18 points, 10 assists and four steals as the Spurs came back from 22 down to beat the Bulls 124-119 — their 10th straight win after an 0-2 start.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The night

The San Antonio Spurs trailed by 22 points midway through the second quarter in Chicago on Wednesday night. The Bulls were 10-for-12 from three, the United Center was loud, and the Spurs looked like a team about to take its first loss in two weeks.

Then they did what they have done all month: they won anyway.

Victor Wembanyama scored 32 points and Dylan Harper — 18 points, 10 assists, four steals — ran the comeback as San Antonio beat the Bulls 124-119, closing out a 4-0 road trip. It was the second night in a row the Spurs had to dig out of a hole, and the second night in a row Wembanyama delivered: he dropped 40 with nine blocks in 25 minutes against Phoenix two days earlier.

The Bulls led 64-42 before the Spurs started chipping away, and Chicago's collapse is its own story. The Bulls have now lost eight straight to fall to 1-9, winless in four home games. Their biggest lead of the season lasted about a quarter.

The history

The record book cares about how the run started, not just how long it has gone. San Antonio opened the season 0-2. Since then, ten wins in a row — and that makes the Spurs just the second team in NBA history to start 0-2 and then win ten straight. The only other club to do it: the 2017-18 Boston Celtics, who turned an 0-2 start into a 16-2 stretch.

That is a very different kind of streak than an undefeated start. Nobody remembers the two losses in October because the response has been perfect since. Ten in a row, and the last one came from 22 down on the road.

What's next

The test gets harder immediately. Golden State comes to San Antonio on Friday night — the same Warriors team that just saw its own eight-game win streak snapped in Houston, and the same team the Spurs beat to start this run's momentum. A win there makes it eleven, and the conversation changes from "nice streak" to "how far can this go?"

Sports · Nov 12, 2026 · 7:54 AM ET

McDavid's point streak hits 20 — only the fourth player ever to open a season like this

By Matt

Connor McDavid picked up an assist in the Oilers' 3-2 overtime win over the Flyers, running his season-opening point streak to 20 games. Only Gretzky, Sundin and Heatley have ever done that.

Disclosure: this post contains affiliate links. I earn a commission on qualifying purchases.

The night

The Edmonton Oilers needed overtime to beat the Philadelphia Flyers 3-2 at Rogers Place on Wednesday, and the game-winner came 47 seconds into the extra session — Evan Bouchard one-timing a feed from Leon Draisaitl short side, off the right post and in. It was Bouchard's 11th goal of the season, the most by any NHL defenseman, and his second overtime winner of the year.

The goal that mattered most for the history books came earlier. Midway through the second period, Connor McDavid found Zach Hyman posted in front of the net on the power play, and Hyman redirected it through Dan Vladar's legs for his second goal of the night. The assist ran the captain's season-opening point streak to 20 games.

Hyman's first multi-goal game of the season could not have come at a better time — he entered the night with one goal all year. Tristan Jarry made 30 saves, and the Oilers improved to 14-3-3, matching the second-best start in franchise history through 20 games. They have won three straight and are 12-0-2 when they score first.

Philadelphia, for its part, did not roll over. The Flyers erased a two-goal deficit on goals from Tyson Foerster and Travis Sanheim to force overtime, and they outshot Edmonton 32-24. They fell to 5-10-6, losers of four of their last five.

The history

Twenty games is where this streak stops being a hot start and becomes a line in the record book. McDavid is just the fourth player in NHL history to record a point in each of his team's first 20 games of a season. The other three: Wayne Gretzky (three times, including the record 51-game run to open 1983-84), Mats Sundin (30 games in 1992-93) and Dany Heatley (22 games in 2005-06).

It is also the second 20-game streak of McDavid's own career — he had one last season, too — making him the eighth player ever with multiple 20-game point streaks. The 20-game mark ties his career high.

The scoring lead is not close anymore. The captain has 49 points — 11 goals and 38 assists — through 20 games, 14 clear of Minnesota's Kirill Kaprizov. For context, he had more points than the Flyers had total goals (45) before the puck dropped on Wednesday.

What's next

The next stop is 21, then Heatley's 22. Sundin's 30 is the realistic horizon; Gretzky's 51 is a different sport. Edmonton starts a six-game road trip Saturday in Toronto, then faces these same Flyers again Sunday in Philadelphia.
